newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis steady to slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis steady to slightly lower.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were mostly steady, although some Kansas bids were slightly softer, grain dealers in the High Plains said Monday.

Warmer-than-normal weather conditions were expected throughout the first half of the week in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas. Meteorology firm Weather Express Inc projected high temperatures Monday in the 70s Fahrenheit in Oklahoma and in the high 60s and 70s in Kansas.
Dealers said the wheat crop was emerging from dormancy thanks to the mild, warm weather.
But there was some concern that if the crop greens up too quickly, it could be prone to damage in the event of a late frost.
"The only bad thing about this weather is that people are worried that if we get a late frost in a few weeks' time, it might damage the crop," a south central Kansas dealer said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
